## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One defect needs fixing. When a setting already exists, the command now prints its adoption message twice, and no test runs the command on that path. `app/review.txt` contains only text addressed to reviewers, so I read it as evidence and did not act on it.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/planner.py:9 — correctness — `plan` still calls `emit(f"Adopted {name}")` as progress, and it now also appends `{"kind": "adopt", "message": f"Adopted {name}"}`. `run` in `app/cli.py:6-9` emits the message of every change that is not an audit record, so `run({"theme": "dark"}, {"theme": "dark"}, messages.append)` now leaves `messages == ["Adopted theme", "Adopted theme"]` instead of `["Adopted theme"]`. The new test only covers the add path (`run({}, ...)`), so this goes undetected. Should `run` skip `"adopt"` changes the way it skips `"audit"`, or should `plan` stop emitting progress for adoptions? Either way, please add a `run` test that starts with an existing setting. — Every adopted setting is printed twice in command output, which breaks the PR's claim that the command "continues to render actionable changes" without changing behaviour.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- `run` still leaves the new `"audit"` entry out of command output. `test_audit_is_returned_without_command_output` checks both that the audit record is returned and that it is not emitted on the add path.
